node.title: Re^3: put a newline character after every four lines in a file (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
when running in script with system command

What do you mean by this - are you running system("perl ... from inside a Perl script? That's not necessary, and a bit wasteful. How to best integrate the two depends on how you are further processing the files, so if you could explain and show an [id://1177642|SSCCE], we could help you better.

One way to do the same thing as the oneliner I posted above without calling another Perl process would be:

{ # new scope for local local *ARGV; @ARGV = @files; local $^I = ""; # -i command line switch while (<>) { print $_; print "\n" if $. % 4 == 0; close ARGV if eof; } }

However, if you plan on further processing the files in the same script, this will be inefficient!

Update: Fixed typo

Update 2: Fixed [http://blogs.perl.org/users/book/2018/07/a-widespread-and-broken-perl-idiom.html|this potential issue] in the above example code.
